51538092.protein: Transient receptor potential cation channel subfamily V member 1
51538092.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human TRPV1 assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: 4.3. Calcium imaging assay Experiments were performed with TRPV1 receptor-overexpressing HEK293 cells. HEK293 cells were grown in 96-well plates at 2 × 104 cells/well in DMEM supplemented with 10 % FBS and cultured overnight. The cells were pretreated with Hank’s balanced salt solution (HBSS) buffer (Gibco, USA) containing drugs and Fluo-4AM (Dojindo, Japan) in a 37 oC incubator for 1 h, washed with HBSS buffer, and then imaged and analyzed using an ImageXpress high-throughput microscope (Molecular Devices, USA).
original_paragraph.SPR Analysis: 2.3. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay To quantify the binding affinity of 10f and 10g to the TRPV1 protein, SPR analysis was used. Both tested compounds bound with TRPV1 in a concentration dependent manner (Fig. 2). As shown in Table 3, the results showed that the Kd value of the lead compound CBD binding to TRPV1 was 110.4 μM. However, the Kd value of modified compound 10f was 40.34 μM, indicating that the binding affinity was higher. Moreover, 10g has the similar activity to CBD in calcium imaging assay, but lower affinity to the receptor in SPR assay. This revealed that the methoxy substitution on the benzene ring can promote the activity. Therefore, in order to determine their pain-relief activities, in vivo experiments are necessary.
